Rashi on Nedarim 16b:1:1.hebrew: מדקאמר חומר בשבועות מבנדרים - כלומר, דזה חומר טפי בשבועות מחומרא דנדרים, מכלל דנדר מיהא הוי כי אמר קרבן לא אוכל לך וכו', דאיסור נדר איכא מדרבנן, אלא דלא לקי מדאורייתא ולא מיחייב קרבן שבועה כי היכי דמחייב בשבועות:
Rashi on Nedarim 16b:1:1.english: Since it states: "A stringency in oaths over vows" - That is to say, that this is a greater stringency in oaths than the stringency of vows — [this implies] by inference that it is at least a vow when one says "An offering [that] I will not eat of yours," etc., in that there is a prohibition of a vow by rabbinic law, except that he does not receive lashes by Torah law and is not liable for an oath-offering as he is liable with oaths.

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:1:2.english: But doesn't [the Mishnah] teach "permitted" - with regard to vows, [meaning] that there is not even any prohibition.

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:2:1.hebrew: אסיפא - הא דקתני "חומר בשבועות מבנדרים", דמשמע דנדר חשיב, לא קאי ארישא דקתני "קרבן לא אוכל לך", אלא אסיפא דאידך בבא (לעיל נדרים יד:), דקתני: "קונם שאיני ישן, שאיני מדבר — הרי זה בלא יחל דברו". ואומר רבינא עלה לעיל (נדרים טו.): לעולם כדקתני "שאני ישן", ומאי "בל יחל"? בל יחל דרבנן, דהיינו איסור דרבנן. אבל שבועה "שאיני ישן, שאיני מדבר" — מדאורייתא אסור, וזה חומר בשבועות מבנדרים, ששבועה חלה על דבר שאין בו ממש וחייב קרבן, מה שאין כן בנדרים:
Rashi on Nedarim 16b:2:1.english: With regard to the latter clause - That which [the mishna] teaches: "[This is] a stringency of oaths vis-à-vis vows," which implies that a vow is considered [valid], does not refer to the first clause, which teaches: "Korban [i.e., an offering], I will not eat of yours," rather [it refers] to the latter clause of the other section (above, Nedarim 14b), which teaches: "Konam [i.e., forbidden] that I will not sleep, [or] that I will not speak — he is [subject] to 'he shall not profane his word.'" And Ravina says regarding it above (Nedarim 15a): Actually, [it is] as [the mishna] teaches, "that I [will not] sleep"; and what [is meant by] "he shall not profane"? A rabbinic [prohibition of] "he shall not profane," which is a rabbinic prohibition. However, [with] an oath "that I will not sleep, [or] that I will not speak," he is forbidden by Torah law. And this is a stringency of oaths vis-à-vis vows, in that an oath takes effect upon something that has no actual substance and one is liable [to bring] an offering [for violating it], which is not the case with vows.

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:3:1.hebrew: אבל מיחל הוא לחפצי שמים - שאם נדר לעבור על אחת מן המצות, אין שבועה חלה עליו, ומיחל לאותה שבועה, דמושבע ועומד הוא לקיימה, ואין שבועה חלה עליו, ויכול לחלל דברו:
Rashi on Nedarim 16b:3:1.english: However, he may profane [it] for the desires of Heaven - For if one vowed [i.e., took an oath] to transgress one of the mitzvot, no oath takes effect upon him, and he may profane that oath, since he already stands adjured to fulfill it; thus no oath takes effect upon him, and he may profane his word.

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:4:1.hebrew: מאי שנא נדר - דאמר כי נדר על המצוה, חל עליו הנדר, וכי עבר ועשה המצוה, קם ליה בלא יחל:
Rashi on Nedarim 16b:4:1.english: What is different [about] a vow - That [it] says [that] when one vows regarding a mitzvah, the vow takes effect upon him, and when he transgresses [the vow] and performs the mitzvah, he stands in [violation of] "he shall not profane [his word]."

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:4:2.hebrew: דכתיב כי ידור נדר לה' - דאפילו בחפצי שמים, דלה' לא יחל דברו:
Rashi on Nedarim 16b:4:2.english: As it is written: "When [a man] takes a vow to the Lord" - [This teaches] that even regarding matters of Heaven [the vow takes effect], for [it is written] "to the Lord, he shall not profane his word."

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:4:3.english: An oath as well - let it take effect upon it [the mitzvah] if one swore to transgress the mitzvah.

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:4:4.hebrew: והכתיב נמי או השבע שבועה לה' לא יחל דברו - דלה' סמוך אאו השבע, דמשמע נמי: לה' השבע שבועה לא יחל דברו:
Rashi on Nedarim 16b:4:4.english: And is it not also written: "Or swears an oath to the Lord, he shall not profane his word" - For [the phrase] "to the Lord" is adjacent to "or swears," so that it also implies: "to the Lord he swears an oath, he shall not profane his word."

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:5:1.hebrew: אמר אביי הא דאמר הנאת סוכה עלי הא דאמר שבועה שלא אהנה מן הסוכה - כלומר, הא דקתני מתניתין שנודרין על המצוה, כגון דאמר "הנאת סוכה עלי", דהשתא קאסר חפצא עליה, דהכי מצי למידר אפי' לכתחילה, כדאמרינן לעיל: אע"ג דמשועבד לאשתו בתשמיש, חל עליו הנדר כי אמר "הנאת תשמישך עלי", שאינו אוסר עצמו עליה אלא לדידה אוסר עליו. וקסבר אביי דבכל לשון שבועה לא מצינו דתיחול עליה, דאי אמר "שבועה הנאת סוכה עלי" דהנאתה אוסר עליו — דהא ודאי לא הויא שבועה אלא נדר, דכיון דקאמר "עלי" היינו נדר, דכל היכא דקאמר "עלי" אמרינן היינו נדר וחייב באחריותו. ונדר הוא כי אמר הכי, אפילו לכתחלה מצי נדר וקאסר חפצא עליה. אבל שבועה לא מצי לאוקמי אלא כגון דאמר "שבועה שלא אהנה", וכהאי גוונא לא חייל עליה, דלא מצי למיסר נפשיה עליה דמצוה כי קאמר "שלא אהנה", דאוסר עצמו במצוה שהוא משועבד לו. וכה"ג מיירי "חומר בנדרים מבשבועות", דבנדרים אומר "קונם הנאת סוכה עלי", ובשבועה "שלא אהנה":
Rashi on Nedarim 16b:5:1.english: Abaye said: This [case refers to] one who said, "The benefit of a sukkah [is forbidden] to me"; that [case refers to] one who said, "An oath that I will not derive benefit from the sukkah" - That is to say, that which the Mishnah teaches, that one may take a vow regarding a mitzvah, [is] such as where he said, "The benefit of a sukkah [is forbidden] to me," for now he forbids the object upon himself — for in this manner he can vow even ab initio, as we said above: even though he is obligated to his wife in marital relations, the vow takes effect upon him when he says, "The benefit of your marital relations [is forbidden] to me," because he does not forbid himself to her, rather he forbids her to himself. And Abaye holds that in no formulation of an oath do we find that it takes effect upon [a mitzvah]; for if he said, "An oath [that] the benefit of a sukkah [is forbidden] to me," such that he forbids its benefit upon himself — that is certainly not an oath, but rather a vow, for since he says "[upon] me," that is a vow, since wherever one says "[upon] me," we say that is a vow and he is liable for its replacement. And it is a vow when he speaks thus; even ab initio he can vow and forbid the object upon himself. However, an oath can only be established [in a case] such as where he said, "An oath that I will not derive benefit," and in such a case it does not take effect upon him, because he cannot forbid himself from a mitzvah when he says "that I will not derive benefit," as he is forbidding himself regarding a mitzvah to which he is [already] obligated. And in such a case [the Mishnah] speaks of "vows are more stringent than oaths," for with vows he says, "Konam, the benefit of a sukkah [is forbidden] to me," and with an oath, "that I will not derive benefit."

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:6:1.hebrew: וכי מצות ליהנות ניתנו - דקאמר הנאת סוכה עלי, הא לא ליהנות ניתנו, ולא מצי למיסר נפשיה בהנאתה, דהא לא חשיבה הנאה מצוה, דלא ניתנו בשביל הנאה:
Rashi on Nedarim 16b:6:1.english: But were mitzvot given for deriving benefit - [Regarding what] he said, "The benefit of a sukkah [is forbidden] to me" — behold, they were not given for deriving benefit, and he cannot forbid himself from its benefit, for a mitzvah is not considered benefit, since they were not given for the sake of benefit.

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:6:2.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא וכו' ישיבת סוכה עלי - כדאמרן, דבישיבת סוכה עלי קאסר חפצא עליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 16b:6:2.english: Rather, Rava said, etc., "Dwelling in a sukkah [is] upon me" - As we said [earlier], for by [saying] "dwelling in a sukkah [is] upon me," he forbids the object upon himself.

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:6:3.hebrew: ובשבועה שלא אשב - קאסר נפשיה מן חפצא, והא לא מצי למיעבד, דמשועבד הוא למצוה, ולהכי לא חיילא עליה שבועה:
Rashi on Nedarim 16b:6:3.english: And [regarding] "an oath that I will not dwell [in the sukka]" - He forbids himself from the object, and he cannot do this, since he is obligated to [perform] the mitzva; and therefore, the oath does not take effect upon him.

Rashi on Nedarim 16b:7:1.english: One might [have thought] that he will be liable - [to bring] an oath-offering.

Tosafot on Nedarim 16b:6:1.hebrew: הא דאמר ישיבת סוכה עלי והא דאמר שבועה שלא אשב בסוכה - פי': היכא דאמר "ישיבת סוכה עלי קונם", מיחל חייל, משום דסוכה אינה משועבדת לו; אבל היכא דאמר "שבועה שלא אשב בסוכה", וגופו משועבד לסוכה, לא חיילא. וא"ת: אדמפליג בנדרים לשבועות, ליפלוג וליתני בשבועו', דבשבועות נמי זימנין דחיילי, היכא דאמ' "ישיבת סוכה עלי שבועה"? וי"ל דאה"נ, אלא אורחא דמילתא קתני, דסתם נדרים החפץ נאסר עליו, וסתם שבועות קאסר נפשיה אחפצא. וה"ק: "זה חומר בנדרים" — מה ששייך בנדרים, דהיינו דקאסר חפצא עליה, ממה ששייך בשבועות, והיינו דקאסר נפשיה אחפצא. ועי"ל: ודאי בשבועות לא חייל בשום צד, אפילו היכא דאמר "ישיבת סוכה עלי שבועה". וטעם גדול יש בדבר: דבשבועות, כיון דסתם שבועות קאסר נפשיה אחפצא ולא קאסר חפצא אנפשיה, א"כ אפילו כשאמר "ישיבת סוכה עלי שבועה", אפ"ה מתרצינן שבועתיה וחזרה על נפשיה, והוי כאילו אמר "שבועה שלא אשב בסוכה". והאי דאמר "ישיבת סוכה עלי שבועה", לא משום דקאסר חפצא עליה — דבודאי בשבועות לא שייך בה — אלא יד שבועה הוי, ולעולם קאסר נפשיה מחפצא; ובנדרים לאידך גיסא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 16b:6:1.english: This [case] is where he said, "Dwelling in a sukka [is prohibited] to me," and that [case] is where he said, "[I take] an oath that I will not dwell in a sukka" - Explanation: Where he said, "Dwelling in a sukka [is prohibited] to me [as] a konam," it takes effect, because the sukka is not bound [to the mitzva] for him; but where he said, "[I take] an oath that I will not dwell in a sukka," since his body is bound to [the mitzva of] the sukka, it does not take effect. And if you ask: Instead of contrasting vows with oaths, let [the Mishnah] distinguish and teach [this] within oaths [themselves], for in [the case of] oaths as well there are times when they take effect, [namely] where he said, "Dwelling in a sukka [is prohibited] to me [by] an oath"? One can answer that indeed it is so, [and] rather [the Mishnah] teaches the usual manner of things: for in ordinary vows the object becomes forbidden to him, whereas in ordinary oaths he forbids himself from the object. And this is what [the Mishnah] is saying: "This is a stringency in vows" — [meaning] that which is characteristic of vows, namely that he forbids the object to himself, [is more stringent] than that which is characteristic of oaths, namely that he forbids himself from the object. And one can further answer: Certainly with oaths it does not take effect in any way, even where he said, "Dwelling in a sukka [is prohibited] to me [by] an oath." And there is a major reason for this: for in [the case of] oaths, since in ordinary oaths he forbids himself from the object and does not forbid the object to himself, therefore even when he said, "Dwelling in a sukka [is prohibited] to me [by] an oath," even so we interpret his oath so that it reverts upon himself, and it is as if he said, "[I take] an oath that I will not dwell in a sukka." And that which he said, "Dwelling in a sukka [is prohibited] to me [by] an oath," is not because he is forbidding the object to himself — for certainly that does not apply to oaths — rather it is a yad [an elliptical expression] of an oath, and he is always forbidding himself from the object; whereas in vows it is the other way around:
